origin:
Proton by Premotion emerged from the vibrant German amateur racing scene in the early 2010s. It was the brainchild of Klaus-Dieter Lehmann, a local garage owner with an insatiable passion for motorsport, and Marcus 'Premotion' Brandt, a talented but underfunded driver. Lehmann, having tinkered with engines since he was a boy, envisioned a team that could punch above its weight, while Brandt craved a platform to showcase his raw talent. Their first car was a heavily modified, second-hand BMW, prepared in Lehmann's small workshop after hours. Their early races were a mix of mechanical failures and flashes of brilliance, but the duo's determination quickly attracted a small but loyal following. 

The team's pivotal moment came at the Nürburgring VLN series. Despite starting near the back of the grid, Brandt skillfully navigated the treacherous conditions, bringing the Proton BMW home in a surprising fourth place. This result not only validated Lehmann's engineering prowess but also secured much-needed sponsorship from a local engineering firm, allowing them to invest in better equipment and personnel. From there, Proton by Premotion slowly but steadily climbed the ranks of the amateur circuit, earning a reputation for being a team that never gives up.
philosophy: Proton by Premotion operates on a philosophy of resourceful innovation and unwavering dedication. Car development is a collaborative effort, with Lehmann's engineering expertise combined with driver feedback from Brandt and the other team drivers. Their approach favors incremental improvements and reliability over radical design changes, as they believe consistency is key to success. The team culture is one of camaraderie and mutual respect, fostering a supportive environment where everyone feels valued and empowered to contribute.
achievements: 4th place at the Nürburgring VLN series (2016)
Multiple podium finishes in regional amateur racing series
Developed and successfully raced a competitive car using mostly second-hand parts
Mentored and developed several young drivers who progressed to higher tiers of motorsport

teamPrincipal.name: Klaus-Dieter Lehmann
teamPrincipal.background: Klaus-Dieter Lehmann is a self-taught engineer with a deep understanding of car mechanics. He is known for his calm demeanor and ability to motivate his team, even under pressure.

keyFigures.name: Marcus Brandt
keyFigures.description: Marcus Brandt is a highly skilled driver known for his aggressive driving style and ability to extract the maximum performance from the car. He also provides valuable feedback to the engineers for car development.

headquarters: Proton by Premotion operates out of a modest workshop located in a small industrial park on the outskirts of Cologne. Their facilities are basic but functional, equipped with essential tools and equipment for car maintenance and repair.
fanBase: Proton by Premotion enjoys a loyal following among local motorsport enthusiasts who appreciate their scrappy spirit and commitment to grassroots racing. Their fans often gather at races to cheer them on, creating a vibrant and supportive atmosphere.
